clue.text: Trump up and about, leg reportedly lifted like a dog's

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
in cricket the leg side is also called the on side

indicators.note: signals that the following words are to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a dog cocks its leg, so a leg lifted that way is cocked

explanation.surface: A rude image of someone fabricating a story while a dog raises its leg nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' means COCKED is heard, giving COCT. 'Trump up' is to invent a false charge or story, nothing to do with the politician.
explanation.definitionFit: To trump up a charge is to fabricate it, the same as cooking up or inventing it.

clue.text: Smelly old dog regularly ran temperature

indicators.note: every other letter of the two words is taken

explanation.surface: An elderly dog stinks and has a fever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes O, D, O from 'old dog'.
explanation.definitionFit: An odorant is something giving off a smell; as an adjective it means odorous.

clue.text: Composition of island cricket club, one short of a team

parts.note: Capri is an Italian island
a cricket team has eleven, one short is ten, written as the letters I and O

explanation.surface: An Italian island's cricket side can only raise ten players.
explanation.walkthrough: Ten is written as IO, a crossword convention mimicking the digits 1 and 0.
explanation.definitionFit: A capriccio is a lively, free-form piece of music, so a musical composition.

clue.text: Wrinkle visible at last after male shuns cosmetics

indicators.note: the visible letter is placed after the trimmed cosmetics in the answer
the male letter avoids the word, so it is removed

parts.note: creams are cosmetic products

indicators.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A man stops using face creams and his wrinkles finally show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shuns' removes M from CREAMS; 'at last' takes E from 'visible', placed after.
explanation.definitionFit: A crease is a line or fold in skin or cloth, the same as a wrinkle.

clue.text: Stupid lapse leads to inept nudist entering A&E

indicators.note: the pieces go into the space between A and E

parts.note: the letters A and E taken as written
a moral lapse is a sin

indicators.note: the leading letters of the following words are taken

explanation.surface: A daft naked person wanders into a hospital's accident and emergency department.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E is a British hospital's casualty department; here it just supplies the outer letters. 'leads to' takes the first letters of 'inept nudist'.
explanation.definitionFit: Asinine literally means like an ass, hence foolish or stupid.

clue.text: Bony, itinerant elks departed northwards

indicators.note: wandering elks have their letters move about
in a down clue going north means reading upwards

parts.note: the late are the departed, the dead

explanation.surface: Wandering elks, gaunt from hunger, head off north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'itinerant' shuffles ELKS to SKEL; 'northwards' reads LATE upwards as ETAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Skeletal describes someone so thin the bones show.

clue.text: Loud individual bitten by Snoopy

indicators.note: the letter is taken in by the other word

parts.note: snoopy means nosy, prying
I is one, an individual

explanation.surface: Someone is bitten by the cartoon beagle Snoopy and yelps.
explanation.walkthrough: Snoopy looks like the Peanuts dog, but it is the adjective meaning prying.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisy and loud both describe making a lot of sound.

clue.text: Old prison of Great Wen put up, then demolished

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means written upwards

parts.note: G is an abbreviation for great
the word is taken as written
to demolish food is to eat it, so ate

explanation.surface: A London jail being built and then knocked down; the Great Wen was Cobbett's name for London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' reverses G and WEN. Newgate was a notorious London prison, demolished in 1904, in the city Cobbett called the Great Wen.
explanation.definitionFit: Newgate Prison stood in the City of London for centuries before closing, so a former jail.

clue.text: Brilliant spies flounder after ill-treatment

indicators.note: the letters are roughly handled and rearranged

explanation.surface: Captured agents struggle after being mistreated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ill-treatment' rearranges SPIES FLOUNDER, all thirteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Splendiferous is a jocular word for splendid or magnificent.

clue.text: Articulate couple foot bill for replacement locks

indicators.note: to articulate is to speak, so the words are said out loud

parts.note: a couple is two, and to foot the bill is to pay

explanation.surface: A pair split the cost of a wig for someone who has lost their hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articulate' here is the verb to speak: 'two pay' said aloud gives the hairpiece.
explanation.definitionFit: A wig worn to cover baldness provides artificial hair in place of hair that has gone.

clue.text: Pretty, half-cut wives frolicking in trailers

indicators.note: half of the word is kept, its first three letters
frolicking wives are jumping about, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Tipsy wives larking about, perhaps at a party on a trailer or in a caravan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' (British slang for drunk) here takes the first half of 'Pretty', PRE; 'frolicking' turns WIVES into VIEWS.
explanation.definitionFit: Film trailers are short previews shown before a movie is released.

clue.text: Using every effort, take drink off total yob

indicators.note: with 'off', removing something from the following word
with 'take', the drink is removed from the word total

parts.note: a tot is a small measure of spirits
a lout is a boorish young thug

explanation.surface: Someone tries hard to deal with a drunk hooligan by taking his drink away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take ... off' removes TOT from 'total', leaving AL. A yob is British slang for a loutish young man.
explanation.definitionFit: Going all out means making the maximum possible effort, an idiom for total commitment.

clue.text: Rottenness of most formidable clearing banks

indicators.note: the banks are the edges of the word, cleared away so the outer letters go

parts.note: the most formidable thing is the scariest

explanation.surface: A bitter remark about the decay at the heart of Britain's big high-street clearing banks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clearing banks' strips the first and last letters from SCARIEST. Clearing banks are the big British high-street banks that settle cheques between themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Caries is the technical term for decay in teeth or bone.

clue.text: Ordinary fruit picker runs yard extremely adeptly

parts.note: Eve picked the forbidden fruit in Eden
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: only the extreme letters, first and last, of the next word are used

explanation.surface: An ordinary fruit-picker dashes around a yard very skilfully.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'fruit picker' is Eve from Genesis, not a farm worker; 'extremely' takes A and Y from 'adeptly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Everyday describes something commonplace, met with routinely.

clue.text: Domestic kitchen full of jam

indicators.note: the words contain the answer within their letters

explanation.surface: A home kitchen crammed with jars of jam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jam' looks like a preserve, but it is the verb: to stick, become fixed fast.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawer that jams gets stuck, so the two verbs share a meaning.

clue.text: Unrealistic statement from seller is edited

parts.note: a seller might say 'I deal'

explanation.surface: A salesman's claim has been tidied up and now sounds too good to be true.
explanation.walkthrough: The seller's statement is read as 'I deal'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something idealised is pictured as perfect, better than reality, hence unrealistic.

clue.text: Throws light on problems besetting posh store

indicators.note: surrounding the other letters on both sides

parts.note: ills are troubles or problems
U means upper-class
a mine is a rich store or source

explanation.surface: Troubles plague an upmarket shop.
explanation.walkthrough: U for posh is the old British label for upper-class usage; 'store' is a rich source, as in a mine of information, not a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: To illumine is to shine light on something, or to clarify it.

clue.text: International organisation says English group not affected

parts.note: UN is the United Nations

indicators.note: the band's name is spoken rather than written

parts.note: Suede are an English rock band

explanation.surface: The United Nations declares that an English group has been unaffected.
explanation.walkthrough: Suede are a 1990s English Britpop band; their name said aloud gives SWAYED.
explanation.definitionFit: Unswayed means not influenced or moved by persuasion.

clue.text: In good health and out of bed, working on stuff

parts.note: someone who has got up is up

indicators.note: the letters are worked over into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A patient has recovered, got up and is busy with things again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' shuffles ON and STUFF into TO SNUFF.
explanation.definitionFit: Up to snuff is an idiom for being up to standard or in good shape.

clue.text: Boxers, for example, partially shampoo chests

indicators.note: only part of the words is used, the answer lying within

explanation.surface: A dog groomer works the lather into the dogs' chests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxers' suggests fighters, but they are dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: The boxer is a breed of dog, and a pooch is a dog.

clue.text: Contractor in bottom of gorge beginning to excavate

parts.note: to gorge or glut is to stuff oneself

indicators.note: the beginning letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A building contractor at the foot of a ravine begins to dig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contractor' is not a builder but a muscle that contracts; 'bottom' is the buttocks, not the base of the gorge.
explanation.definitionFit: The gluteal muscles of the buttocks contract to move the hip, so a muscle in one's behind.

clue.text: Proposition Mother Courage ultimately abandoned

indicators.note: wild, unrestrained letters are rearranged
the ultimate, final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Brecht's play Mother Courage, and the heroine abandoning her children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives E; 'abandoned' shuffles MOTHER and E.
explanation.definitionFit: A theorem is a mathematical proposition to be proved.

clue.text: They cross water using this motorway

indicators.note: the words are put to use in a new order

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI

explanation.surface: A traveller takes the motorway because it crosses a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is Britain's first motorway; 1 becomes I. 'using' shuffles THIS and MI.
explanation.definitionFit: Isthmi are narrow land strips running between two seas, linking land across the water.

clue.text: She has loan of drill, welcoming din

indicators.note: one word takes the other into its middle

parts.note: a borer is a tool for drilling
a row is a loud noise

explanation.surface: A woman borrows a power drill and puts up with the racket.
explanation.walkthrough: ROW in the sense of noise rhymes with 'cow'.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who has taken out a loan is someone who borrows.

clue.text: Set out incense back to front

indicators.note: the back letter moves to the front

parts.note: to incense is to anger

explanation.surface: An instruction to place sticks of incense the wrong way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incense' is the verb to anger, not the perfume; R moves from back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: To range things is to arrange or set them out in order.

clue.text: Silly smile is easier after losing weight

indicators.note: a letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: simpler means easier
L stands for a pound weight, from libra

explanation.surface: Someone grins foolishly because life is easier after a diet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing weight' looks like dieting; it means taking out L, the pound (from Latin libra).
explanation.definitionFit: A simper is an affected, coy and foolish smile.

clue.text: See 12
Much obliged to a hunky jockey

indicators.note: to jockey is to manoeuvre about, so the letters are moved around

explanation.surface: Gratitude expressed to a handsome jockey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jockey' looks like a rider; here it is the verb meaning to shift about.
explanation.definitionFit: Much obliged is a polite phrase of gratitude, an expression of thanks.

clue.text: State of Orbán leaving American wanting to scoff

indicators.note: the letter departs from the word

parts.note: Viktor Orbán is the prime minister of Hungary

explanation.surface: A political jibe: Orbán's country turns away from the Americans and wants to mock them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scoff' looks like jeering; here it is to eat greedily.
explanation.definitionFit: A hungry person wants to eat, scoff being slang for wolfing food down.

clue.text: Rises up and starts to attack savage Conservative objectives

indicators.note: the starting letters of the following two words

parts.note: ends are aims or objectives

explanation.surface: Political opponents rise up to assault Conservative aims.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts to' takes A and S from 'attack savage'.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascend is to climb or go upwards.

clue.text: Attractive twins come to repudiate origins

indicators.note: the words disown their original letters, so each loses its first

explanation.surface: Charming twins arrive and reject their family background.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repudiate origins' drops T and C, the first letters of 'twins' and 'come'.
explanation.definitionFit: Winsome means charming and appealing, often in an innocent way.
